# T13 authored extraction acceptance evidence

Observed locally on 2026-10-06. This is a bounded synthetic quality measurement,
not a production-distribution, complex-layout, or speech-recognition benchmark.

## Authored gold and criteria

Before corpus parsing/OCR, `manifest.json` froze 20 files and manually written
source labels. SHA-256:
`a12c02b759f4485b20effb6920634906d6cbe05102d0ac73945175382b499c7a`.
Each fixture SHA-256 is stored in that manifest and checked by the test.
No gold was derived from parser output or relaxed after execution.

Eight ledger formats (TXT, PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, HTML, EPUB, ODT) require the
exact ordered sequence of authored Unicode letter/number tokens, both
paragraphs in order, and all six table cells in row-major order. PDF/PPTX have
two labeled pages. Punctuation and whitespace are layout separators: this
measurement does not establish exact punctuation or geometric layout fidelity.
Unicode TXT additionally requires byte-exact preservation, including emoji.

Additional cases cover empty TXT, corrupt PDF/DOCX/EPUB, empty/encrypted PDF,
invalid UTF-8/NUL TXT, scanned PDF without automatic OCR fallback, actual
English image OCR, and an unavailable Whisper backend. A deterministic
1,540,096-byte Unicode TXT is generated inside the test and compared exactly.
Valid empty text is distinguished from parser errors and unavailable backends.

English OCR uses whitespace-only normalization, preserving case/punctuation.
Predeclared limits are CER <= 0.05 and WER <= 0.10; authored numeric facts
17/23/40 must match exactly. Same/dropped-word/wrong-digit/Unicode controls
verify zero and nonzero edit-distance scoring. Exact numeric assertions were
strengthened after the initial score-only probe; source gold and its hash were
unchanged. The final runs below exercise both numeric and scoring checks.

## Native measurements

Tesseract 5.5.3 with installed `eng` data; other installed languages are `osd`
and `snum`, with no `rus` quality measurement. No downloaded model, remote
provider, forced PSM setting, or stub transcription was used.

Final English OCR result:

```text
Copper count 17. Zinc count 23. Total units 40.
CER = 0 / 47 = 0.000000
WER = 0 / 9  = 0.000000
Exact numeric facts = [17 23 40]
```

The labeled WAV was generated by installed local Fred TTS: PCM signed 16-bit,
16 kHz, mono, 5.643750 seconds. Whisper quality is **UNMEASURED** because no
engine endpoint is configured. Its test checks the unavailable-backend error;
it does not claim a successful transcription. The scanned-PDF empty-text
boundary is likewise not an OCR quality pass.

Both generated PDF pages were rendered with pdftoppm 26.09.0 and visually
inspected: readable table, unclipped English/Cyrillic paragraphs and correct
page order. Render inspection files are temporary `/tmp/levara-t13-ledger-page{1,2}.png`.

## Observed commands

```sh
LEVARA_T13_TESSERACT=1 go test -p 1 -ldflags=-w -count=1 -json ./pkg/extract ./pkg/chunker -skip '^TestMemoryREST'
LEVARA_T13_TESSERACT=1 go test -race -p 1 -ldflags=-w -count=1 -json ./pkg/extract ./pkg/chunker -skip '^TestMemoryREST'
```

Both commands exited **0**. Final GREEN: extract 79/79 test nodes passed,
1.251 seconds; chunker 54 passed / 1 existing skip, 0.193 seconds. Final race:
extract 79/79 passed, 4.123 seconds; chunker 53 passed / 2 existing skips,
1.194 seconds, no race report. These counts include existing tests and parent
nodes; they are not counts of independent document fixtures.

Existing skips: `TestChunkBookParity` requires an external book fixture;
`TestChunkBySliding_LargeText` additionally skips its timing threshold under
race. The new large-text retention test itself passed both final runs.

Raw final logs: `/tmp/levara-t13-final-green.jsonl` and
`/tmp/levara-t13-final-race.jsonl`. Initial corpus run selected no chunker tests
and skipped actual OCR; neither is substituted for the final commands above.

## Diagnostic regression and limits

The deterministic successful CLI process emitted source text on stdout and a
resolution warning on stderr. Before the parent-owned production correction,
the warning appeared in extracted text: focused command exited **1**, extract
0.830 seconds (`/tmp/levara-t13-ocr-stderr-red.jsonl`). Root fixed success to
consume stdout while retaining failure diagnostics. The final test confirms
both successful text isolation and nonzero-exit stderr preservation. Its POSIX
process fixture explicitly skips on Windows; no Windows runtime claim is made.

Parent-owned corrected CLI hash:
`8307faa571504dd8c06ae6884cddc5aae7fcafd2d84d7e05c8a5abf8ae478ed0`.

Residual measurements: noisy/rotated scans, Russian OCR, real speech, Whisper
accuracy, complex document layouts and production workload distributions.
These are unmeasured, not silently accepted. Existing report binaries and
production extraction code were not modified by this corpus worker.

## Root current gate and acceptance

Root `make test-ocr` exited 0 with `LEVARA_T13_TESSERACT=1`: native extraction
plus CGO-disabled test-binary compilation for darwin amd64/arm64, linux amd64,
windows amd64/arm64. Cross-compilation does not establish OCR execution on those platforms.

Final component terminal leaf counts: GREEN 130 passed / 1 existing skip;
race 129 passed / 2 existing skips / zero race reports. Independent review
checked current source, all 20 fixture digests, authored gold and raw final logs;
no bounded must-fix remained.
